title: Sherpa: workload-signature-driven batching advisor with continuous safe-apply
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build an adaptive recommendation service (Sherpa) that synthesizes lightweight workload signatures and rules to propose safe continuous batching and caching parameter adjustments to reduce inference unit cost while preserving latency SLOs.

Hypothesis: many routes show stable micro-patterns (high prefix reuse, predictable length distribution, bursty windows) that enable modestly larger batching windows or relaxed max_tokens-per-batch without increasing p95 latency beyond SLO. Applied conservatively and continuously, these adjustments reduce token cost by 6-18% for eligible workloads.

Telemetry & Workload profiling: extract compact daily signatures per route and model variant: average seq_len, seq_len_std, prompt_prefix_reuse_ratio, kv_cache_hit_rate, inter-arrival time quantiles (p50/p95/p99), burst_fraction (requests in 1s windows), tail latency baseline (p90/p95/p99), and error rate. Retain 14 days of examples for rolling comparisons. Primary data sources: route-level traces in Console (tracing tags), metric export pipeline (Prometheus -> BigQuery), and sampling of actual request payloads stored in secure S3 (redacted).

Heuristics engine: start with deterministic rules encoded as weighted selectors: e.g., if prefix_reuse_ratio > 0.65 and kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.40 and burst_fraction between 0.05 and 0.25 => recommend increase batch_window_ms by +25% up to 150ms; otherwise propose microbatch_size cap adjustments. Heuristics are intentionally conservative and bounded by safety constraints. Each rule emits expected cost delta, estimated p95 shift, and confidence score derived from signature similarity to historical successful applies.

Continuous parameterization and safe-apply plan: Sherpa runs in two modes: "Shadow" (simulation) and "Controlled apply". Shadow mode replays live traces against simulated batching configs to validate cost/latency tradeoffs offline. Controlled apply uses a staged rollout: 0.1% traffic shadow apply -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> global apply. Each stage requires passing health gates for 30m: no increase in route error rate >0.5 percentage points, p95 latency less than 120% of SLO or absolute increase <30ms, and user-level tail-quantiles (if available) not regressing. Failure triggers immediate rollback and postmortem.

Rollbacks and safeguards: rollback triggers include: sustained error rate uplift, p95 latency breach beyond thresholds, new spike in customer-facing 500s, or observed model hallucination increase for structured outputs (monitored via eval hooks). Sherpa maintains a compact provenance record for every apply (signature snapshot, rule version, telemetry baseline, rollout stages). All applies are idempotent and reversible via stored previous config.

Operational metrics and acceptance criteria: primary metrics: cost-per-1k-tokens change, p95 latency delta per route, route error rate, successful apply rate, and rollback frequency. Acceptance: for targeted routes the expected cost decrease >= 5% with p95 latency increase <= 5% absolute or within SLO limits in steady state. Rollback rate must be < 2% of applies in the first 90 days.

Testing strategy: unit tests for heuristics, synthetic workload simulation harness built on existing replay infra (ENG-30911), end-to-end shadow runs on staging with historical traces, and canary experiments. We will add chaos tests (introduce synthetic bursts and KV cache evictions) to validate safety.

Implementation outline: lightweight controller service (Go) that consumes signatures from pipeline, runs rules, emits recommendations to Console and a config change API. A small operator in the runtime reads approved configs and orchestrates the staged apply using existing rollout primitives (canary/traffic-split). Initial heuristics in Python as a notebook for rapid iteration; rewrite core rule engine in Go for production.

Docs and artifacts: design brief (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sherpa+Batching+Advisor (internal), prototype notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/sherpa-prototype, staging replay dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sherpa-shadows. Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2871 (shadow harness), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/662 (recommendation UI).

Risks & trade-offs: overaggressive batching risks tail-latency regressions and customer-visible errors; conservative rules limit cost wins. Profiling can miss short-lived but important workload shifts; we mitigate with rolling windows and continuous shadowing. Shadow simulations are not perfect; therefore controlled canary and short-stage monitoring are critical.

Next steps: finalize heuristics DSL, wire up signature export (ENG-7421 dependency), build staging shadow runner (ENG-30911), create replay dashboards, and land initial canary control flow.

Acceptance criteria: demo that Sherpa recommends safe config for 5 routes in staging reducing cost-per-1k-tokens by >=5% without p95 regression during 48h shadow; PRs merged for shadow harness + minimal UI for approvals.
